system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Seller Document Review: Departures from Playbook & Push‑Back Plan

---

## 1. Executive Summary
The Seller’s “FINAL” package is **not** agreed. Every material term departs from the playbook—most critically on liability caps, thresholds, time limits, fundamental warranties, fraud carve‑outs, disclosure, buyer knowledge, Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, employee bonuses, Ironquay IP, and title evidence. The Seller’s “REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE” and “PREAMBLE” are tactical framing devices; they do not bind us. We must issue a comprehensive mark‑up rejecting the [STANDARD] labels and re‑opening every item.

---

## 2. Clause‑by‑Clause Departures & Reasoning

| # | Playbook Position | Seller Draft | Departure & Risk | Reasoning |
|---|-------------------|--------------|------------------|-----------|
| **1** | **General Cap: 25% / AUD 6M** (20% / AUD 4.8M *only* with Amelia Frost written authority—**none given**) | 20% / AUD 4.8M (Clause 12.1) | **Hard cap 33% below our opening; fallback used without authority.** | The playbook treats 20% as a *conditional* fallback. No principal sign‑off exists. Accepting this silently concedes AUD 1.2M of protection. |
| **2** | **De minimis AUD 5k; Basket AUD 50k (first‑dollar recovery once exceeded)** | De minimis AUD 25k; Basket AUD 250k (excess‑only recovery) (Clause 12.2) | **5× higher thresholds; “excess‑only” vs “first‑dollar” shifts AUD 200k+ risk to Buyer.** | Market “standard” cited by Seller is irrelevant—our mandate is stricter. The basket gap alone exposes Buyer to AUD 200k of unrecoverable claims. |
| **3** | **General claims period: 24 months** (18 months *only* with Amelia Frost approval—**none given**) | 18 months (Clause 12.3/13) | **6 months shorter; no approval obtained.** | SaaS latent defects (IP, data privacy, tax) often surface after 18 months. |
| **4** | **Fundamental/Title: Separate regime – 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** | “Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity” | **Total collapse of fundamental protection into the weak general regime.** | Title/capacity defects are binary and catastrophic; they must sit outside all general limitations. |
| **5** | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: Carved out of *all* caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non‑reliance** | “Limitations, exclusive‑remedy and non‑reliance provisions apply to *all Claims of any nature*” (Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5) | **Fraud/intentional misconduct would be capped, time‑barred, and subject to non‑reliance.** | Unenforceable in NSW to the extent it excludes fraud, but the clause creates litigation risk and chills claims. Must be expressly carved out. |
| **6** | **Disclosure: Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole‑data‑room, public‑register, prudent‑search deemed disclosure** | General disclosure of entire data room (DD‑002–DD‑012) + public registers + statutory registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2) | **Boilerplate “dump” disclosure shifts due‑diligence burden to Buyer; playbook requires granular, specific disclosure.** | NSW courts require “fair disclosure” (identifiable, specific). Whole‑room disclosure is ineffective for warranty qualification. |
| **7** | **Buyer knowledge: Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier = named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity** | “Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” (Clause 8.3) | **“Discoverable” standard is objectively broader than actual knowledge; wipes out claims for anything in 10,000+ page data room.** | Playbook forbids blanket buyer‑knowledge qualifiers. This clause would bar claims even for matters Buyer did not actually know. |
| **8** | **Bluefen: Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied *before* Completion. Reasonable endeavours insufficient for material customer consent** | “Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent” (Clause 3/6.3). *No final consent or condition‑satisfaction evidence in data room (Disclosure 2)* | **No certainty Bluefen will consent; conditions (cl. 11.3) unverified. Post‑completion consent failure = lost 30% revenue.** | Material customer consent must be a hard condition precedent, not a reasonable‑endeavours obligation. |
| **9** | **Riverlark: Current payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective security releases. Post‑completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** | “Release to be provided *following* Completion” (Clause 2/7). *Facility not repaid; no discharge (Disclosure 3)* | **AUD 3.2M debt remains on Target; security not released. Buyer inherits refinancing risk.** | Playbook requires pay‑off at Completion from purchase price. Post‑completion promise is unsecured and unenforceable without irrevocable undertaking. |
| **10** | **Employee bonuses (DD‑005): AUD 420k + on‑costs = specific line item or Seller‑funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them** | “Bonuses are a matter for the Seller and are *not separately itemised* in the funds flow” | **AUD 420k + payroll tax/super/on‑costs (~AUD 80–100k) disappear from price mechanics.** | If not deducted from price or funded by Seller, Buyer effectively pays twice (once via price, again via post‑completion payroll). |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP: Broaden narrow indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure. AUD 180k not independently verified** | “Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment considered adequate” (Clause 11.1). *No receipt/assignment in data room (Disclosure 4)* | **Narrow indemnity leaves Buyer exposed to IP ownership/third‑party claims beyond SOW3 fees.** | Playbook requires broad IP indemnity; SOW3 cure is a separate commercial issue. Payment unverified—risk of double payment. |
| **12** | **Export/Privacy Incident (DD‑006): Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty, or numeric demand** |
=== END ADVICE ===
